newsitem.title: FRANCE: Luxury group LVMH shows small H1 profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Luxury group LVMH shows small H1 profit rise.

text.p: French luxury goods group LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton said on Thursday its profit rose 5.4 percent in the first half of 1996 but operating income fell.
Its profit excluding exceptional items rose to 1.54 billion francs ($300.6 million) , on the low end of analysts' expectations, from 1.46 billion.
But operating income fell to 2.61 billion francs from 2.92 billion, reflecting a slump in profit in the perfume and cosmetics division as the group battled counterfeit versions.
Investors, disappointed by the mixed results at one of France's most successful groups, hammered the share in early trading on the Paris bourse.
LVMH's stock was down 2.45 percent at 1,074 francs at 0830 GMT after having fallen 2.8 percent on Wednesday on nervousness ahead of the results.
The company, whose brands range from Christian Dior perfumes to Pommery champagnes and Louis Vuitton luggage, said operating income in all its other divisions rose in the first half.
It said the operating results were helped by brisk luggage sales in the summer, stable cognac sales in Japan and higher wine and champagne prices.
"LVMH maintains its objective for growth in sales and net income for 1996 as a whole," it said in its first-half earnings statement. ($ = 5.122 French Francs)
